newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks slip at open after gold fades.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks slip at open after gold fades.

text.p: Australia shares opened slightly weaker on Monday with resource issues depressing an otherwise neutral market after the price of gold neared four year lows on offshore markets on Friday.
At 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 1.5 points weaker at 2,711.5.
The June share price index was three points lower at 2,719 and at a 7.5 point premium to the underlying index.
Stocks were mixed with the gold sector pulling resources lower but support for a few blue chip industrial issues helping to balance the market overall.
"This is the week of the rumble when they (institutions) value their portfolios and nothing else matters," a dealer from a Sydney-based brokerage said.

The dealer said historical analysis of the Australian market indicated that fundamental factors typically have not made a significant impact on the market in the week leading up to the June 30 balance date.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corp was among the better performing issues, the media group's shares continuing to rise after it announced a deal to sell its U.S. satellite TV assets earlier this month.
News Corp ordinary shares were 12 cents higher at A$6.40 (US$4.80) while its preferred stock was 13.3 cents higher at A$5.31.
Gold issues opened nearly all weaker, the gold index 19.5 points or 1.3 percent weaker at 1,482.7.
The most active issues early were building materials company James Hardie Industries and Australia's largest listed company, the Broken Hill Pty Co (BHP).
BHP shares opened slightly weaker in line with the market. The oil, steel and minerals giant is due to release its earnings for the the year to May 31 at the end of the week.
